text:
mia: FYI cluster ap-southeast1 had a spike in gpu attach failures at ~04:20 UTC. quick triage points to local SSD (nvme) write bursts during janitor async-rewrite phase.
sam: sample dmesg from gnode-apse1-066: 
```
[  260.400101] nvme nvme0n1: write timeout, aborting
[  260.400220] writeback: I/O error, dev nvme0n1
[  260.401000] provisioner: scratch alloc timed out
```
mia: iostat during spike: %util ~98, avgqu-sz high.
leo: we pushed janitor_parallel=10 yesterday; that will multiply concurrent rewrites per host.
anya: blast radius: ~28% attach failures across the regional preemptible pool for ~6m. no public customer impact but internal batch backlog grew.
sam: short-term plan: 1) throttle janitor_parallel -> 3 on a 6-host canary 2) apply per-host soft iops cap of 55k wkB/s 3) add routing fallback to eu-west for new gpu requests while rolling.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 created: "ap-southeast1 nvme iops saturation -> gpu attach stalls" (severity: medium)
leo: opened PR to add iops-aware backoff in janitor: https://git.internal/redwood/janitor/pulls/478
mia: canary flipped, nvme util dropped to ~40% within 90s, attach success rate returned to normal. expanding rollout.
sam: cost note: routing to eu-west increases cost ~15-20% for affected jobs; prefer config rollback if stable. :thumbsup:
